record.paper_title: Twenty Open Problems in Enumeration of Matchings: Progress Report
record.original_question: Let f(n) denote the number of perfect matchings of the n-dimensional cube. Determine the sequence f(n) modulo 2^m for arbitrary positive integers m.

evidence.quote: The claim follows, and similar albeit more complex reasoning should allow one to compute the enumerating sequence modulo any power of 2.

artifact.self_contained_problem: For each positive integer $n$, let $Q_n$ denote the graph of the $n$-dimensional hypercube, whose vertex set is $\{0,1\}^n$ with edges joining pairs of vertices differing in exactly one coordinate. Let $f(n)$ denote the number of perfect matchings (1-factors) of $Q_n$. For every positive integer $m$, determine the sequence $\bigl(f(n) \bmod 2^m\bigr)_{n\ge 1}$ in closed form (e.g., as an eventually periodic function of $n$, or via an explicit congruence/recurrence describing $f(n)$ modulo $2^m$).
artifact.status_search_result: The exact value of f(n) is known only for small n (computed up to n=7 via dynamic programming), and the sequence appears as OEIS A005271. No general closed-form description of f(n) modulo arbitrary powers of 2 was found in the search results; only the suggestion that such a description should be obtainable in principle is recorded, but no published proof for general 2^m was located.

status_evidence.title: A005271 - OEIS
status_evidence.snippet: Number of perfect matchings (or dimer coverings) in the n-cube.
status_evidence.claim: The sequence f(n) is tracked but only finitely many terms are known explicitly.

status_evidence.title: Enumerating Perfect Matchings in n-Cubes
status_evidence.snippet: Dynamic programming approach used to obtain the total number of perfect matchings in the 7-cube.
status_evidence.claim: Computational, not closed-form, results are the state of the art.
